newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel offers rise on back of crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel offers rise on back of crude.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run began the week stronger on the back of crude's gains with more sellers on the market asking higher numbers for July barrels, traders said.
A major sold a small parcel of 0.4 pct max material late on Friday at a steady $104 fob. The 8,000-tonne cargo was sold out of Scandinavia and was bought by a local.
For 0.5 to 0.7 pct straight-run sellers were a little more active on the market, all asking three figures in line with gains made by crude futures.

A refiner was offering its mid-July material at $102 fob -- or $1 up on Friday -- and a second seller, a Scandinavian refiner, said it would only accept bids above $100 fob for its July barrels from Gottenburg.
A third seller said he was looking for about $101 for his July low sulphur straight-run, adding that a potential buyer, a major, was still mulling its position but may do a deal later this week.
Buyers were at $98/$99 and some interest was coming in from some three U.S. players.
"Outright prices are up on the back of crude," one trader said. Others seconded this view.
Russian high sulphur straight-run was on offer at steady prices but buying interest was said to be thin.
Traders said some E-4 and M-40 straight-run cargoes were on offer at three means plus $3.5/$5 and three means plus $5 respectively and three M-100 cargoes at two means plus $1.50/ $2.
